title: fix(tools): reject apply_patch Add File when target already exists
body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to Cline!
-->

### Related Issue

**Issue:** #13833

### Description

#### Problem
`apply_patch` **Add File** silently overwrites files that already exist on disk. The intended behavior is to throw `Add File Error: File already exists`, but that guard was never reached for Add-only patches.

#### Root cause
`loadFiles()` preloaded only the paths behind `*** Update File:` and `*** Delete File:` headers, so an `*** Add File:` target was never present in the `currentFiles` map that `parseAdd()` checks. When the add path was already on disk, `fs.writeFile` simply replaced it.

#### Fix
`loadFiles()` now also attempts to read `*** Add File:` targets. If the file exists, its content is loaded into `currentFiles`, which lets the existing `parseAdd()` guard reject the patch with `Add File Error: File already exists`. If the file does not exist (`ENOENT`), the optional load is skipped, preserving the normal "create new file" path.

#### Verification
- Added a regression test in `apply-patch.test.ts`: an existing `note.txt` plus an Add File patch throws and the file content is unchanged.
- Focused unit test run: `bunx vitest run src/extensions/tools/executors/apply-patch.test.ts --config vitest.config.ts` — 11/11 passing.
- `bun -F @cline/core typecheck` passes.
- `bun run biome check --diagnostic-level=error` on the two changed files passes.

#### Risks
- Update/Delete behavior is unchanged: those paths are still loaded in the required-file loop and still throw `File not found` when missing.
- The add-path load is best-effort and only treats `ENOENT` as expected; any other read error is still rethrown so permission or I/O problems do not go unnoticed.

title: feat(llms): sampled cline-provider AI SDK tracing via the host OTLP exporter
body:
### Related

Stacked on #13851 (retarget to `main` when it merges). Client half of the Langfuse collector relay: cline/infra#547 (prod) adds the collector pipeline that forwards only `ai.model.provider ^cline` spans to Langfuse. Activation (env values in publish builds) is deliberately separate: #13982.

### Description

Today AI SDK telemetry only turns on when Langfuse credentials exist in the process (`LANGFUSE_*` env), which external clients never have — so no external client emits gen-ai spans. This PR adds the second enablement path and covers **every execution host** (whichever process runs `streamText()` emits the trace):

| Surface | Execution | Trace owner |
|---|---|---|
| VS Code | local | extension host |
| CLI (fallback/yolo/sandbox) | local | CLI process |
| CLI (normal, hub-routed) | hub | detached daemon |
| Desktop sidecar | hub | detached daemon (sidecar deliberately gets no tracer) |
| Hub dashboard/chat/scheduled | hub | detached daemon |

In three parts:

**Extension/host half** — the VS Code extension gains a TracerProvider: when `tracesExporter` is configured, spans batch-export over OTLP (grpc / http/json / http/protobuf) to the same collector endpoint as logs/metrics. `tracesExporter` is plumbed through all three config sources: build constants (`OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`), runtime env (`CLINE_OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`), and remote config (`openTelemetryTracesExporter` — controls only the remote-config-owned extension tracer, not build/runtime tracers). The CLI build inlines the new envs alongside the existing OTEL set.

**Hub daemon half** (merged in from #14034) — the daemon spawns detached from the same compiled binary as the CLI, so the publish build's inlined env activates it for free; transport, flush-on-shutdown, and telemetry flow to the hub server and scheduled runs all pre-existed. What it adds is identity: spans carry only the OTel resource, so the daemon now declares `serviceName: "cline-hub-daemon"` (+ version) via new optional fields on the shared config — otherwise daemon traces are indistinguishable from CLI-local ones. Opt-out holds unchanged (same-machine, same-user process; shared topologies tracked in ENG-2525).

**SDK half** — `resolveAiSdkTelemetry(providerId, samplingKey)` decides per stream:

1. **Direct Langfuse path unchanged** — env credentials present → enabled, full content, every request (hub/internal behavior today).
2. **Collector relay path** — cline/cline-pass only, and:
   - **One export path per host**: the direct Langfuse path declines whenever a host OTLP tracer is registered, so a process configured with both `LANGFUSE_*` credentials and the relay emits each span once, never twice.
   - **Honors the user's telemetry opt-out.** Spans bypass the `ITelemetryService` wrapper that enforces opt-out for events/metrics, so this path re-checks the shared global settings file (`telemetryOptOut`) per stream — covering startup state and mid-session opt-outs across extension and CLI. The check **fails closed**: only a genuinely absent file (first run) reads as opted in; malformed JSON or any other read failure disables the relay. Opted-out users emit no trace spans, period.
   - A host that registered a traces exporter defaults to **100% task sampling**; `CLINE_TRACE_SAMPLE_PERCENT` reduces it (0 disables). No workflow sets the exporter yet, so shipped builds keep tracing dark until #13982.
   - Sampling is a deterministic FNV-1a hash of the task/session id (`sessionId` → `conversationId` → `distinctId` from request metadata), so whole tasks sample together — never per-request fragments — and retries decide identically. Below 100% with no key: stays off.
   - **Content recording is a build-time flag, off in code**: `recordInputs`/`recordOutputs` default false; `CLINE_TRACE_RECORD_CONTENT=true` turns on full prompt/completion capture. The rollout ships content ON from the first activation — #13982 bakes both the exporter and the content flag into publish builds (data-governance sign-off happens on that PR). There is no metadata-only phase planned; the flag exists so content can be disabled without touching this code.

### Test Procedure

From the worktree:

```text
bun -F @cline/llms test -- src/services/langfuse-telemetry.test.ts   # 21/21 passed
bun -F @cline/llms typecheck                                          # clean
bun -F claude-dev check-types                                         # clean
bun biome check <changed files>                                       # clean
```

New coverage: direct-path passthrough, provider boundary, **global opt-out respected (and direct path deliberately unaffected)**, default-100% with tracer, explicit-0 disables, metadata-only default, content opt-in, deterministic sampling (kept and dropped buckets stable across calls), keyless sub-100% stays off, no-tracer stays off.

### Type of Change

-   [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
-   [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
-   [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
-   [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes
-   [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes
-   [ ] 📚 Documentation update

-   [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs)
-   [x] Relevant tests are passing and changed code is formatted and linted
-   [x] I have reviewed the contributor guidelines

### Screenshots

Not applicable — SDK/telemetry behavior only.

### Remote tracer lifecycle and validation

- Carry `openTelemetryTracesExporter` through schema validation and state transformation. **Coordinate API-server schema deployment** before using the field.
- Retain trace-only clients in both factory and remote-config paths; wrappers own client disposal. Removal/clear awaits shutdown before replacement.
- Disposal clears the relay marker and releases only the owned global tracer slot. Re-enable/endpoint replacement succeeds; rejected registrations are shut down without displacing another owner, and disposal awaits that cleanup.
- Tested enable → disable → re-enable, endpoint replacement, async parent/child context, cached-tracer shutdown, foreign-owner protection, schema mapping, and retention/cleanup failures.
- Validation: 1,114 extension unit tests across 79 files; 27 SDK telemetry tests; extension TypeScript check and esbuild bundle passed.
- Operational runbook: `apps/vscode/src/services/telemetry/providers/opentelemetry/RUNBOOK.md`. Remote config is **not** a universal no-release kill switch.

### Additional Notes

This PR ships completely dark: nothing is emitted anywhere until a host registers the OTLP traces exporter, which no publish workflow does until #13982. Build-time rollout knobs require a rebuilt release; runtime environment changes require restarting the operated process. Remote configuration can disable only its own extension tracer after fetch/apply, on clients with this fix and after coordinated API-server schema deployment. It does not disable the build-configured tracer activated by #13982, CLI/hub tracing, or direct Langfuse export. Collector sampling/exporter changes are no-client-release mitigation for Langfuse forwarding, not client emission; allow for deployment propagation and queued/in-flight spans.

title: fix(llms): wire per-call Langfuse telemetry and isolate direct export
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #13479

Stacked on #13974 (`alex/cline-provider-collector-traces`). Carries the necessary per-call integration and isolated exporter ownership from the superseded #13650. Retarget to `main` after #13974 merges.

### Description

With #13974, a credential-free AI SDK v7 stream resolves telemetry to enabled but emits zero spans: the relay never supplies an integration. A regression using the real AI SDK, Langfuse integration, and in-memory OpenTelemetry exporter reproduces this on the parent branch even though its 27 telemetry unit tests pass.

Pass the selected Langfuse integration through `telemetry.integrations` for every enabled stream. Relay calls acquire the current host tracer so provider replacement redirects subsequent requests. Direct `LANGFUSE_*` export uses an isolated tracer provider, and cleanup flushes and shuts down only SDK-owned exporters. This also prevents direct initialization from registering integrations globally or claiming a host's tracer slot.

Preserves #13974's Cline/ClinePass-only boundary, relay precedence over direct credentials, per-stream global opt-out, deterministic task sampling, and content-recording flag. A previously cached direct integration cannot bypass a subsequently registered relay's policy. Credentials continue to work for Cline providers when no host relay is active.

### Test Procedure

- `bun run build:sdk` — passed.
- `bun run typecheck` in `sdk/packages/llms` — passed.
- LLM telemetry unit tests: 23 passed; real-stream integration tests: 8 passed; AI SDK provider tests: 37 passed.
- Core host telemetry tests: 23 passed across `OpenTelemetryProvider.test.ts` and hub daemon `telemetry.test.ts`.
- Extension tracer lifecycle tests: 4 passed.
- Biome on changed TypeScript/package files and `git diff --check` — passed.

Coverage includes metadata-only output, explicit content capture, mid-session opt-out, excluded providers, deterministic sampling, tracer replacement, direct/relay coexistence, unrelated AI SDK calls, host ownership, and standalone async trace context.

### Additional Notes

title: fix(desktop): keep voice input errors in chat instead of opening settings
body: ### Related Issue **Issue:** #XXXX (small bug fix; no linked issue) ### Description **Issue:** Clicking the microphone can take the user to Settings → Voice even though a voice provider and transcription model are already selected. This interrupts the chat and hides why speech input failed. **Root cause:** The composer’s speech-input error handler treated every error other than a browser `DOMException` or `Event` as a reason to open Voice settings. A connection or transcription failure therefore triggered the same redirect as an assumed configuration problem. The microphone is already gated on a configured transcription target, so this redirect did not indicate that the model selection was missing. **Fix:** Show a “Speech input failed” toast in chat with the actual provider/recording error. Remove the unused Voice-settings callback from the composer and its parent components. ### Test Procedure - Composer regression suite: 40 tests passed (`bunx vitest run webview/components/views/chat/chat-input-bar.test.tsx --config vitest.config.ts`, from `apps/examples/desktop-app`). - Desktop TypeScript check passed (`bunx tsc -p tsconfig.dev.json --noEmit`). - UI build and formatting completed; `git diff --check` passed. - Added regression coverage for a transcription connection error and a microphone permission error with a configured voice model. Both verify the toast, retained draft, and available microphone button. - Manual follow-up: select a voice model, enter a draft, trigger a speech-input failure, and verify chat remains visible with the error toast. title: fix(llms): correct OpenCode Go session headers and model API routing
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** [ENG-2522 — OpenCode doesn't work](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/ENG-2522/opencode-doesnt-work)

### Description

OpenCode Go requests now carry a stable conversation ID and use the API protocol declared for the selected model. This addresses the reported `Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently` failure and the transport mismatch found while investigating Muse Spark's `Internal server error`.

**Root causes**

- Go requires `x-opencode-session` to stay stable within a conversation and a client-specific User-Agent. Cline's required-header handling covered Cline billing and Codex, but not Go; Go also had not opted into the gateway's existing sticky-session support.
- The Go provider defaults to OpenAI Chat Completions. Models.dev declares different adapters through model-level `provider.npm`, but catalog normalization discarded that field. Consequently, Muse Spark requests went to `/chat/completions` instead of `/responses`. MiniMax models likewise need the Messages adapter.
- Several Go Qwen catalog entries omit the adapter declaration even though Go documents an Anthropic Messages endpoint.

**Fixes**

- Add Go's session and client headers to shared session setup. Enable gateway sticky-session headers for direct gateway callers using `metadata.sessionId`; retries reuse the same identity. The builtin also supplies a Cline User-Agent.
- Preserve model adapter declarations as typed `metadata.apiProtocol` through catalog normalization and both builtin/live model projections. Refresh the bundled Go routing metadata and catalog version so the fix works before a live catalog refresh.
- Let HTTP gateways opt into per-model protocol routing under their shared base URL. Go opts in; other providers and local CLI transports retain their existing behavior. The selected adapter handles serialization, provider options, and stream parsing, rather than rewriting only the URL.
- Add a narrowly scoped Go Qwen fallback when upstream omits `provider.npm`. Explicit upstream declarations take precedence.

| Go model | API route |
| --- | --- |
| GLM, Kimi | `/chat/completions` |
| Muse Spark, GPT, Grok with OpenAI adapter declarations | `/responses` |
| MiniMax, Qwen | `/messages` |

title: feat(desktop): list Cline Pass with Cline and add a set-up row to the composer provider picker
body:
### Related Issue

Follow-up to #14021 (the configured-provider indicator), prompted by reviewing what a brand-new Cline Pass user actually sees in the composer.

### Description

Three related changes to the composer's provider picker, all driven by the same fact: **the picker only lists providers that have a saved `providers.json` entry.** That's `enabledProviderIds` in the webview, which the sidecar derives from `enabled = Boolean(directSettings)` in `listLocalProviders` — literally "does an entry exist for this id".

**1. Cline Pass now lists alongside Cline.** Desktop onboarding signs in with `provider: "cline"` and never writes a `cline-pass` entry. Cline Pass stores its credentials *under* `cline` (`storageProviderId: "cline"` in the auth registry), so the one sign-in genuinely configures both — `getProviderSettings("cline-pass")` already resolves the shared auth, and Settings already shows Cline Pass as Configured. But the composer keyed on entry-existence, so a fresh Cline Pass user saw exactly one row: Cline. `listLocalProviders` now marks a provider enabled whenever the provider it stores credentials under is enabled. This is symmetric by construction: a `cline-pass` sign-in writes the `cline` entry (that's where the token goes) and then `markLocalProviderEnabled("cline-pass")`, so Cline was already covered in that direction.

The CLI's provider picker inherits this — it treats `enabled` as `isConfigured` — so Cline Pass now reads as configured there too when Cline is. That matches reality.

**2. A "Set up another provider" row at the bottom of the picker.** Since the picker is by construction "what you've set up", it's the natural place to reach the rest of the catalog. The row is a sentinel option (`__add-provider__`) with a `Plus` icon; `handleProviderSelect` intercepts it and calls `onOpenModelSettings` — the same callback the welcome-state "connect a model" notice already uses to open Settings → Models — instead of selecting. It's an action, not a selection: `onProviderChange` is never called and the trigger keeps showing the current provider. It only renders when the callback is provided, so existing callers that don't pass it are unaffected. On the compact (<560px) layout it also closes the mobile menu, since the settings view overlays it.

I went with a sentinel option rather than adding a footer slot to `SearchCombobox` deliberately: it gets keyboard navigation, `Enter`, search-highlighting, and close-on-select for free, and doesn't need a new UI-package prop. The one quirk is that a search query filters it like any other row — which reads as reasonable.

**3. Reverts #14021's green "Configured" check on the picker rows.** For anyone who set their providers up in the app, every row satisfies `isProviderConnected` and gets the same check — decoration, not information. The two predicates only diverge on entries with no usable credentials (legacy VS Code migration seeding, empty saves, sign-outs that leave the entry behind). That *is* worth surfacing, but Settings already does it per provider and has the affordance to fix it; the composer doesn't. The `indicator` prop on `SearchCombobox` goes too — the picker was its only consumer. `isProviderConnected` itself stays; Settings, voice input, and the first-run notice still use it.

#### Gotchas found along the way

- `Boolean(directSettings)` is a weaker predicate than it looks: a `cline` entry persists after sign-out (the auth block is blanked, not the row), so a signed-out user still sees Cline — and now Cline Pass — in the picker. That's pre-existing behavior for Cline and the change keeps the pair consistent; the turn fails with the normal credential-failure hint.
- `resolveProviderSettings` merges the storage provider's `auth`/`apiKey`/`baseUrl` under the alias's `provider` id, which is why `configured` and `oauthAccessTokenPresent` were already `true` for Cline Pass while `enabled` was `false`. The fix only had to touch `enabled`.

### Test Procedure

- `sdk/packages/core` `local-provider-service.test.ts`: 97 pass, including two new cases — Cline Pass is `enabled: true, configured: true, oauthAccessTokenPresent: true` from a `cline`-only sign-in with **no** `cline-pass` entry on disk, and stays `enabled: false` when there's no `cline` entry either.
- Desktop webview `chat-input-bar.test.tsx` + `provider-model-catalog.test.ts`: 45 pass, including a new test that opens the picker, asserts the rows are exactly `["Cline", "Cline Pass", "Set up another provider"]`, clicks the last one, and checks `onOpenModelSettings` fired once, `onProviderChange` never did, the trigger still reads Cline, and the panel closed.

title: fix(desktop): stop rendering a deleted queued prompt in the chat
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #14038

### Description

Deleting the first queued prompt in the desktop app made it show up in the chat as a user message that never ran.

The sidecar's `pending_prompts` handler in `sidecar/context.ts` inferred that the head of the queue had started running whenever a snapshot arrived with fewer items and a different head, and emitted `chat_queued_prompt_start` for the old head (which is what renders the user bubble). Deleting the first queued prompt, or discarding the queue on abort, produces exactly that snapshot shape, so the removed prompt was announced as started.

The runtime already emits `pending_prompt_submitted` for every real start (`drain` and `consumeSteer` in `PendingPromptsController`), and the sidecar already translates that into `chat_queued_prompt_start`. This PR drops the snapshot-diff heuristic and relies on `pending_prompt_submitted` alone. The per-session id dedupe in `emitQueuedPromptStart` is kept.

### Test Procedure

Automated:
- Added a regression test in `sidecar/context.test.ts`: a `pending_prompts` snapshot with the head removed and no `pending_prompt_submitted` must not emit `chat_queued_prompt_start`, while `prompts_in_queue_state` still reflects the remaining queue. It fails on `main` (one start event emitted for the deleted prompt) and passes with the fix.
- The existing "announces a queued prompt start once when drain emits both queue events" test still passes, confirming real drains are still announced via `pending_prompt_submitted`.

title: fix(core): persist seeded sessions with their live idle status
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #14037

### Description

In the desktop app, a forked session got stuck on "Thinking..." after restoring a checkpoint and switching away from and back to the session.

Root cause: sessions seeded with history (forks, checkpoint restores) materialize their row and manifest eagerly at start via `ensureSessionPersisted`, but that call never passed the session's status, so `createRootSessionWithArtifacts` fell back to its `"running"` default while the live session was actually `"idle"`. A checkpoint restore reuses the session id and resumes from the persisted manifest, so the restored session came back with a stale `"running"` status. The webview's hydration then saw `running` plus a transcript ending on a user message and showed the working indicator indefinitely.

Fix: pass `status: session.status` when persisting the row. One-shot and prompted sessions are unaffected (they start as `running` already), and the first turn still transitions through `markTurnRunning`.

### Test Procedure

- Extended the existing `persists seeded history at session start` test in `local-runtime-host.test.ts` to assert the row is created with `status: "idle"`. Verified it fails without the fix and passes with it.
- Reproduced the issue end to end in the headless desktop app (sidecar + web UI in Chrome) following the exact steps from the issue: run a task with two turns in a git workspace, fork the session, restore the first checkpoint in the fork, switch to the original session, switch back. Before the fix the forked session showed a stuck "Thinking..." spinner and the composer read "Agent is working...". The persisted session row/manifest showed `status: running` with no prompt. title: fix(schedules): prevent polling stalls and default to local timezone  CLINE-3224
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** [CLINE-3224 — Fix daily schedule running multiple times each morning](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3224/fix-daily-schedule-running-multiple-times-each-morning)

### Description

Daily schedules could create repeated sessions for one logical run, start at unexpected times, or stop making progress behind unfinished work. This PR fixes polling and lease ordering, makes claiming respect shared database capacity, cancels interrupted execution safely, and preserves schedule timing during creation and editing.

**Issues, root causes, and fixes**

| Issue | Root cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One unfinished run blocks later schedules | Startup awaited the initial batch before installing its timer; `tick()` held the polling guard until all turns finished. | Install polling before initial dispatch and release the guard before awaiting executions. |
| Sleep/wake creates another attempt of a locally active run | Polling can resume before heartbeats and reclaim an expired lease. | Renew locally active claims before querying expired work. |
| Busy schedules starve unrelated work and inflate waiting-run attempts | The first 25 queued siblings are repeatedly claimed and rejected by an in-memory limiter. | Apply global and per-spec capacity inside the SQLite claim transaction, before selecting the next row. Waiting work stays unclaimed with no false errors or attempts. Remove the separate in-memory limiter. |
| Separate runners exceed `maxParallel` | Each runner has its own concurrency counters. | Count live claims in the shared database and re-evaluate capacity after each claim in the same write transaction. |
| Work starts after shutdown, or a stale worker keeps executing | Shutdown requeued runs without draining startup/turn promises. Lease loss only stopped heartbeats, and session attachment was not claim-bound. | Track cancellation and execution promises, abort on shutdown/lease loss, drain execution with bounded cleanup, clean up late startup responses without sending a turn, and require the current claim token for session attachment. |
| A configured timeout does not stop hung startup | Only `sendSession` was timed out. | Apply one deadline across request preparation, startup, and the turn; bound each cleanup operation to five seconds. |
| Report failures replay already completed work | Both success and error paths wrote reports before persisting terminal status. A second report failure left the row running until lease expiry. | Persist the execution outcome first; log report failure independently and do not replay the turn. Only the current owner publishes completion or updates run-related state. |
| New schedules use an unexpected timezone | Desktop omitted timezone, service defaults were implicit, and agent guidance allowed guessed zones. There is no hardcoded EST default in this path. | Send the desktop's current IANA timezone; default omitted recurring timezones to the scheduler host's local zone at creation. Preserve explicit and existing timezone choices, including an absent timezone, and instruct the agent not to guess. |
| Editing a prompt changes an advanced cron expression | Daily/weekly controls discard fields or steps from expressions they cannot represent. | Preserve the original expression when timing values are unchanged; display the saved expression and explain that timing changes replace it. |

Graceful shutdown now records interrupted active runs as **cancelled**, rather than automatically replaying work that may already have performed external actions. Explicit retries remain possible. Crash recovery still uses expiring leases; this is not an exactly-once guarantee for external side effects.

Optional scheduler telemetry records camelCase trigger kind, attempt count, start delay, duration, and outcome, including cancellation and superseded ownership. Prompts, paths, and raw errors are excluded. Report and cleanup failures have separate structured logs; telemetry capture failures cannot stop execution.

### Test Procedure

Use disposable schedules and rebuild/restart the SDK and app/hub when switching revisions. Running processes do not hot-reload SDK changes. Screenshots alone do not establish the teammate's complete sleep/wake sequence; the tests below reproduce individual implementation failures deterministically.

**Manual: unfinished work and blocked siblings**

1. Create Schedule A with `maxParallel: 1` and a task that stays active for several minutes, such as waiting for a five-minute command to finish before responding. Confirm its turn actually remains active; a detached command followed by an immediate response does not exercise this behavior.
2. While A is running, create Schedule B with a one-time execution approximately one minute in the future and a short prompt.
3. Wait past B's due time and two polling intervals (15 seconds each by default). On the original main implementation, B waits for A's entire batch. With this PR, B starts while A remains active, provided global capacity is available.
4. For the backlog regression, queue more than 25 additional **Run now** executions of A before making B due. With the earlier independent-polling implementation, blocked siblings fill every claim batch and B remains queued. With this PR, B runs, and waiting A siblings retain zero attempts and no concurrency error.
5. Let A finish and verify its queued siblings can progress.

**Manual: sleep/wake**

1. Start a long-running schedule and record its logical run and session.
2. Sleep the laptop longer than the default 90-second lease, then wake it while the same hub process remains alive.
3. Confirm the same live execution is not reclaimed as another attempt and unrelated due work can progress.

The hazardous poll-before-heartbeat ordering is nondeterministic on real hardware. The regression test forces the lease into the past before polling and verifies the original run remains at one attempt.

**Manual: timezone and preserving advanced cron**

1. In a desktop environment whose local IANA zone is not New York, create a new 9 AM recurring schedule without requesting an explicit timezone. Inspect the saved timezone and next occurrence: they should match the desktop zone.
2. Explicitly choose another timezone through the API/agent and confirm that choice is retained. Existing schedules, including timezone-less schedules, must keep their saved timezone behavior during unrelated edits.
3. Create a recurring schedule through the API/agent with `0 */2 * * *` (every two hours), or `0 9 1 * *` (monthly).
4. Open it in desktop settings, edit only its prompt/name, and save. Inspect `cronPattern`: it must remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Before this fix, these examples become daily schedules.
5. Change the timing controls and save again. The expression should now reflect the selected daily/weekly timing; the editor displays the original expression and explains this replacement.

**Deterministic lifecycle and storage reproductions**

These cases use temporary databases/workspaces and deferred fake runtime handlers, avoiding real provider calls or external side effects:

- **Shutdown during startup:** keep `startSession` unresolved, call `stop()`, then resolve startup. Previously a prompt was sent after stop while the row was queued. Now the run is cancelled, the late session is cleaned up, no turn is sent, and no session ID is attached afterward.
- **Shutdown during a turn:** keep `sendSession` unresolved, stop the runner, then resolve the old promise. Verify abort/cleanup, terminal cancellation, and no automatic reclaim. Also keep abort/stop handlers unresolved and advance fake timers to prove shutdown is bounded.
- **Startup timeout:** configure a one-second timeout and hold startup open past the deadline. Previously the row remained running. Now execution fails at its deadline, checks elapsed wall time when resuming before an overdue timer, releases its active tracking, and cleans up a late session without dispatching a turn.
- **Report failure:** replace the temporary report directory with a regular file. Exercise both a successful turn and a provider failure. Verify the original outcome is terminal and cannot be reclaimed after the lease interval.
- **Shared capacity:** use two store connections/runners against one database. Hold one schedule active and queue another execution with `maxParallel: 1`; the second runner must not start it. Separately verify the database-wide global limit across connections and capacity release after completion.
- **Lease loss:** expire an active worker's lease and claim its run from another worker. Poll the original runner and verify it aborts without overwriting the replacement claim, attaching a stale session ID, or writing a stale report.

**Validation run**

- `bun run build:sdk` — SDK/UI builds.
- From `sdk`: `bun -F @cline/core test:unit src/cron src/services/telemetry/core-events.test.ts src/ClineCore.test.ts src/hub/server/agenda-task-hub.test.ts` — 177 scheduling, telemetry, lifecycle, and hub integration tests.
- From `sdk`: `bun -F @cline/core typecheck` — core and smoke typechecks.
- From `apps/examples/desktop-app`: `bun run typecheck` — desktop typecheck with its UI build prerequisite.
- From desktop: `bunx vitest run webview/lib/routine-schedule-cron.test.ts webview/lib/routine-schedule-timezone.test.ts --config vitest.config.ts` — eight cron preservation/timezone tests.
- Biome checks on changed TypeScript/TSX files and `git diff --check`.

The preceding PR commit passed the SDK CI jobs on both Ubuntu and Windows. New commits trigger fresh CI; the local checks above do not claim a completed full monorepo test run.

### Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] ♻️ Refactor Changes
- [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes
- [x] 📚 Documentation update
- [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes

- [ ] Tests are passing (`bun test`) and code is formatted and linted (`bun run format && bun run lint`)
- [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

The builds, targeted tests, typechecks, and formatting checks listed above were run; the full monorepo test/lint commands were not run.

### Screenshots

The editor adds a text note showing the saved cron expression. No new screenshot is attached; expression preservation is covered by the focused tests above.

### Additional Notes

- Based on `main`; excludes the separate provider-model-refresh changes.
- This does not keep a sleeping laptop awake or move execution to the cloud. No new default run timeout is introduced; configured timeouts now cover startup as well as the turn.
- Graceful shutdown cancels active runs. Abrupt process failure still falls back to lease-based recovery, so external actions should tolerate retries. Runtime handlers that ignore cancellation cannot be forcibly terminated by the scheduler.
- New recurring schedules retain their captured IANA timezone if the host timezone later changes. Existing timezone-less schedules retain their dynamic local behavior. Remote callers should supply the user's intended timezone explicitly.
- The SDK is still in development: concurrency now belongs to database claiming and the unused `ResourceLimiter` export is removed; session attachment requires a claim token.
- The separate event-ingress durability finding is outside this daily scheduling fix and is not included here.

title: fix(desktop): clear legacy Codex credentials on ChatGPT sign-out
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** [CLINE-3233](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3233/sign-out-doesnt-work-for-codex-provider) Sign out doesn't work for Codex provider

### Description

Signing out of the ChatGPT Subscription (openai-codex) provider in the desktop app did nothing: the "Signed in via browser" state came right back.

Root cause: `ProviderSettingsManager` re-runs the legacy `globalState.json` / `secrets.json` import in its constructor, and the desktop sidecar constructs a new manager for every command. Sign-out (`save_provider_settings` with `enabled: false`) deletes the provider entry from `providers.json`. The next sidecar command saw `openai-codex` missing, found `openai-codex-oauth-credentials` still in the legacy extension's `secrets.json`, and re-imported the tokens.

Fix (temporary, desktop only): when the desktop app signs out of `openai-codex`, also remove `openai-codex-oauth-credentials` from the legacy `secrets.json`, so there is nothing for the import to bring back. Other keys in that file are left alone. This is a stopgap until the legacy import is retired; the fuller cleanup is to stop re-running the import on every manager construction.

### Test Procedure

- New `sidecar/legacy-codex-credentials.test.ts`: removes only the Codex key and keeps the rest; no-op when the file is missing or has no Codex key.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.dev.json --noEmit` for the desktop app: clean. `biome check`: clean.
- End to end with `dev:sidecar` + `dev:web` and an isolated `CLINE_DIR` seeded with a classic-extension style `secrets.json` (Codex OAuth creds plus an unrelated OpenRouter key) and a `globalState.json` selecting `openai-codex`. On startup both providers were imported and showed as Configured. Clicking Sign out on ChatGPT removed it, and after a full page reload it stayed "Not configured" while OpenRouter stayed Configured. On disk, `secrets.json` afterwards contains only the OpenRouter key.
